subject: Urgent: adaptive QPS oscillation — mitigation plan and customer note
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FastRetail reporting adaptive QPS oscillation — urgent triage + customer note request

Team —

FastRetail (FR account) just flagged repeated latency spikes and a throughput oscillation on their Gen-API route between 08:40–09:00 PT. They see ~8–12s tails intermittently for completion endpoints; p50 is fine but p95/p99 spiking. They provided a short log snippet (attached) and have traffic pattern that auto-bursts from their checkout flows.

What I need:
- SRE: quick triage to confirm whether this is runtime/KV cache eviction/queueing or a model scheduling problem. Any immediate mitigations we can run (route-level throttling, short-term scaling)?
- Product: short-term tolerance change or config we can push to reduce request fanout; any quick config that doesn't require a rollout?
- Customer comm: I want to send a concise customer-facing note within the hour acknowledging, high-level cause (if known), and ETA for remediation. Draft attached as cust-brief-v1.docx — please edit.

Context: FastRetail is on a Reserved Dedicated pool with burst capacity enabled but they are near their burst cap; if we need to expand for ~2 hours we will need approval from commercial for a temporary credit.

Logs attached: qps-sample-logs-20280516.txt (trimmed).

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 May 2028 09:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastRetail reporting adaptive QPS oscillation — urgent triage + customer note request

Rachel — quick update from triage:
- We've reproduced a pattern where rapid fanout of small completion requests combined with sequence-length variance triggers scheduling backpressure on the dedicated pool. KV cache hit-rate dipped (~18% -> 4%) during the burst window, which increased decode time and exposed a scheduling queue.
- No model OOMs observed; GPU utilization climbed but did not saturate across the pool.

Immediate mitigations we can push (low-risk):
1) Short-term route-based concurrency cap: set max_concurrency=8 for the customer's primary gen route. This will bound fanout and reduce scheduling queueing (rollback in 30m if stable).
2) Enable aggressive KV prefetch for their most common prefix (cheap at runtime) — requires per-account config flip, no deployment.
3) If those don't relieve tail, request a temporary burst-cap increase (we can flip +2 nodes into their pool if commercial approves).

I'll apply #1 and #2 now as a canary to a single region; monitoring in Datadog and our per-route traces.

Attachments: applied a short collect trace to INF-4532 (link below).

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 May 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastRetail reporting adaptive QPS oscillation — product config + roadmap note

Thanks Ben — this matches a pattern we saw in other checkout-burst customers. Two quick product asks / clarifications:

1) Concurrency cap behavior: please confirm that the cap will queue at the Redwood gateway (not drop) and that we'll preserve request ordering for the customer's calls. We should include that in the customer note.

2) Short-term config for KV prefetch: good. Can we make the prefetch scope limited to their highest-frequency prompt set to avoid memory pressure? If yes, that's the recommended short-term mitigation.

Roadmap/longer term (for post-mortem): we need a guided setting in Console that suggests per-route caps based on historical fanout patterns and a Burst Insurance product (predictive temporary capacity) to avoid manual commercial approvals. I'll log a short RFC and include perf metrics from this incident for prioritization.

Also: Commercial will need a stub message (one-liner: temporary burst seats requested) — Rachel, loop in Sales Ops if you want me to ping.

Marissa Cole
Group PM, Serving
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 May 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FastRetail — brief update on reported latency spikes

Samir — quick note while we triage: we see the elevated tails on your Gen-API route and are actively applying targeted mitigations.

What we have done so far:
- Applied a temporary concurrency cap and aggressive KV prefetch for the most common checkout prompts.
- Monitoring shows initial reduction in p99 tail within 12 minutes in the canary region; we are observing across regions now.

Next steps / ETA:
- We expect to have a stability read at ~13:00 PT and will update you then. If the mitigation does not fully resolve it we will request a brief temporary capacity bump for your dedicated pool to cover the remainder of the peak.

We appreciate the quick signal and will keep you posted.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: cust-brief-v1.docx (internal draft)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 May 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastRetail reporting adaptive QPS oscillation — mitigation outcome and next steps

All — final status and recommended follow-ups: 

Outcome from canary: p99 reduced from ~9.4s -> ~2.1s on canary region after concurrency cap + scoped KV prefetch. No downstream errors observed. KV hit-rate recovered to ~52% for the prefetched prefix.

Immediate follow-ups (owners):
- Commercial: Rachel to request temporary +2 burst nodes if the customer requests continued burst capacity; product will provide a limited runbook for approval (Rachel/Marissa).
- Product: Marissa to create Console suggestion for per-route cap (RFC INF-4601).
- SRE: Ben to run a 2-hour watch and capture traces for post-mortem.
- Account: Rachel to send the customer wrap note by 15:30 PT with the brief summary and offer to request burst capacity.

Customer note draft (suggested one-paragraph to send):
"Thanks for flagging — we identified that a rapid fanout pattern during your checkout window reduced our KV cache hit-rate and increased per-request queuing. We applied a temporary concurrency cap and a targeted KV prefetch which shortened the observed latency tails; we will continue to monitor and can provision brief additional capacity if you prefer. Expect another update by 15:30 PT"

I'll keep monitoring and will post our post-mortem in INF-4532.

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Runtime
Redwood Inference
